name: MonarchTableBlock
title: TableBlock
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout inside androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll; androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField per editable cell; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu for the controls
summary: A small table of text inside a document: a read-only form that scrolls sideways, and an editable form with a text field per cell and a menu to add and delete rows and columns.
whenToUse: For a short table of text in an article, a note or a document editor: prices, a comparison, a schedule.
whenNotToUse: For a large or sortable data set use a data grid or a lazy list. For a list of key and value pairs use a description list.
api: @Composable fun MonarchTableBlock(data: MonarchTableBlockData, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, caption: String? = null, label: String? = null, labels: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels())

@Composable fun MonarchTableBlock(data: MonarchTableBlockData, onDataChange: (MonarchTableBlockData) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, caption: String? = null, label: String? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, labels: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels(), onDelete: (() -> Unit)? = null)

class MonarchTableBlockData { val rows: List<List<String>>; val hasHeaderRow: Boolean; val rowCount: Int; val columnCount: Int; val canAddRow: Boolean; val canAddColumn: Boolean; val canDeleteRow: Boolean; val canDeleteColumn: Boolean; operator fun get(row: Int, column: Int): String; fun isHeader(row: Int): Boolean; fun withCell(row: Int, column: Int, text: String): MonarchTableBlockData; fun withHeaderRow(hasHeaderRow: Boolean): MonarchTableBlockData; fun addRow(after: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun addColumn(after: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun deleteRow(at: Int): MonarchTableBlockData; fun deleteColumn(at: Int): MonarchTableBlockData }

MonarchTableBlockData.Companion: const val MAXIMUM_ROW_COUNT = 50, const val MAXIMUM_COLUMN_COUNT = 20, fun of(rows: List<List<String>>, hasHeaderRow: Boolean = true): MonarchTableBlockData, fun empty(rowCount: Int = 3, columnCount: Int = 3, hasHeaderRow: Boolean = true): MonarchTableBlockData

class MonarchTableBlockLabels(region: String? = null, controls: String? = null, addRow: String? = null, addColumn: String? = null, deleteRow: String? = null, deleteColumn: String? = null, headerRow: String? = null, deleteTable: String? = null, emptyCell: String? = null, cellPosition: ((row: Int, column: Int) -> String)? = null)

options.name: data
options.description: The cells and whether the first row is a header.

options.name: onDataChange
options.description: Editable overload: called with the new table after every change.

options.name: caption
options.description: Text above the table. Also its spoken name.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the table when the caption is not the right one.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Editable overload: whether the cells and the menu respond.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Editable overload: adds "Delete table" to the menu. The app removes the table.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Cells are text. Columns are 96dp to 240dp wide at the default font size and the text wraps inside them.

states.name: editable
states.description: Every cell is a text field in a 144dp column, at least 48dp high, and a "Table" button above the table opens the menu.

states.name: header row
states.description: The first row has the subtle background, the strong body style and the heading semantics. Switched in the menu or with withHeaderRow.

states.name: at a limit
states.description: Add row is disabled at 50 rows, add column at 20 columns, delete row and delete column at one.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Editable overload with enabled = false: the text uses the disabled color and the fields and the button do not respond.

appearance: The table has a 1dp border in the default border color with 8dp corners and 1dp lines between cells. Body cells sit on the surface color, header cells on the subtle background; the caption uses the caption style in muted text. Each role has its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component is a scrolling frame for an HTML table and a Tiptap node built on prosemirror-tables. Android has no block editor, so, as on iOS, the editable form is a self-contained composable over a MonarchTableBlockData value that a block editor can host later; the data type has the web's commands (add row below, add column after, delete row and column, header row) and limits (50 by 20). Not offered: selection across several cells, merged cells (colspan and rowspan), rich text inside a cell, and Tab to move between cells (the keyboard's own Next and focus navigation apply). The web shows the controls only while the caret is in the table; here the "Table" button is always above an editable table and acts on the cell that last had focus, or on the last row and column. The data is an immutable value with onDataChange, where iOS takes a Binding. Column widths grow with the font size setting, up to twice.
accessibility: The scrolling frame is a traversal group named by label, else the caption, else "Table"; a caption that is the spoken name is hidden from TalkBack so it is not read twice.
The grid carries collection info (rows and columns) and every cell its row and column, so TalkBack can announce the position.
A read-only cell is read as its text, or "Empty".
Header cells are headings and use the strong body style, so the header does not depend on its fill.
An editable cell is a text field whose content description is its position, "Row 2, column 1".
The controls are a MonarchButton and a Material 3 DropdownMenu; the header row item has the checkbox role and its state; "Delete table" is in the danger text color.
Editable cells are at least 48dp high, the button has a 48dp target, and text grows with the font size setting.
edgeCases: Ragged rows are padded with empty cells; an empty input becomes one empty cell; rows past 50 and columns past 20 are dropped.
Reading a cell outside the table gives an empty string; changing one returns the same value.
After a row or column is added, its cell at the target takes focus; after a delete, the nearest cell does.
At the largest font size the columns are wider and the table scrolls sooner.
The grid is not lazy: it is meant for small tables, which the limits enforce.

An editable table

MonarchTableBlock(
